quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. They may be marked with horizontal lines, vertical lines, or both. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same thing as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop and yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a certain number of passengers.
Specific turning movements are allowed from specific lanes.
Do not enter.
Drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is reserved for vehicles with a certain number of passengers.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane sign. HOV lanes are reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more distance between your vehicle and the vehicles ahead.
Approach all vehicles with caution.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the distance between your vehicle and others because slippery roads require more time to stop.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go through in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog reduces visibility of other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive cautiously at reduced speed. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better in fog.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions may pass if it is safe and they will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop immediately. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely.
Not watching carefully for workers and equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down for traffic conditions and keep distance from other vehicles. Pay close attention to workers and equipment.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with limits on stereo volume.
A TV show.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, back, and front. Cars in these spots cannot be seen. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road space.
Demand the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road space.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, give vehicles traveling toward you at least half of the road. Both vehicles need adequate space to pass safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that hospital emergency services are located to the right.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered gates.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross, since trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park.
Places where you must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and instructions from flaggers. Only cross when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-lane road unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe passing on a two-lane road requires that you can see ahead clearly, return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle has the speed to pass safely. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you know where other vehicles are near you.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in before turning left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane that is closest to where you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge to the right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
A road is entering from the left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a yield sign is coming. Start slowing down when you see this warning sign.

questions.question: If you need to stop or slow down suddenly, and the driver behind you may not expect it, what should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn constantly.
Wave your left arm out the window.
Tap the brake pedal quickly several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Tap your brake pedal three or four times quickly. Your brake lights will alert other drivers that you are slowing down.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is beginning.
There is a higher chance of seeing pedestrians.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times it is posted. The "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" can happen when you:

options.text: Stare straight ahead at the road for a long time.
Take frequent rest stops.
Get too much sleep the night before driving.
Take short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stare straight ahead at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop looking at the road around you. You may zone out and not notice traffic slowing down ahead of you.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and be ready to yield or stop before turning.

questions.question: If you have a probationary license or instructional permit, when can you use your cell phone while driving?

options.text: If you are just answering a call.
As long as you don't text.
Only when reporting an emergency.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when reporting an emergency.
questions.explanation: In Wisconsin, you cannot use a cell phone while driving if you have a probationary license or instructional permit. The only exception is to report an emergency.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Require your vehicle to need a tune-up sooner.
Make you drowsy while driving.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases and cools hot gases from the engine. A leaky exhaust system releases dangerous fumes that can make you drowsy and cause serious harm.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden under the seat.
Stops the seat belt buzzer or light from working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with enough room to fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you see this hand signal.

questions.question: You must use your low beams anytime you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use your low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off wet surfaces and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: If the traffic light is red and you want to turn right, you can turn:

options.text: When the cross traffic has cleared.
After you stop.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Unless there is a sign that says you cannot, you may turn right at a red light after coming to a complete stop. You must yield to other traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists before turning.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less grip your tires have. If you drive too fast, your tires will hydroplane—slide on a layer of water instead of gripping the road.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: To merge safely, find a gap large enough for your vehicle to enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: If you face a green traffic light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, you should:

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if other vehicles are blocking it, even if your light is green. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light changes, you will block cross traffic and can be ticketed.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive using your four-way flashers.
Drive using your parking lights.
Not turn on any vehicle lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic or 500 feet of traffic ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian on the roadway and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at a steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you need to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
Traffic is moving in both directions.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in both directions.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about two-way traffic.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed with care.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery and dangerous when wet. You could lose control of your car. Slow down on wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking a non-prescription drug?

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Continue driving no matter what the label says.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. Always check the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: When must you stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When you cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
When the crossing is in a city with frequent trains.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time, going either direction. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts affect highways?

options.text: They only affect large vehicles.
They only cause visibility problems.
They can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers. It can blow dirt and dust into the road, lowering visibility. Wind can also physically move your vehicle.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
When you can see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you are far enough from the other vehicle. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the lane divider is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What can bad suspension cause?

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: A red light is showing, but a police officer tells you to go through. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions. They override traffic signals and signs.
